sentences.text: JUDGMENT
This claim petition is filed under Sec.166 of M.V Act, 1988 seeking compensation for the death caused in a Road Traffic accident.

2. The case of the petitioners in the nutshell is that, on 24.04.2023 at about 8.20 a.m, the deceased went to Gudibande along with Gangappa in his TVS Bike bearing Reg.No.KA-03- ES-7366 slowly and cautiously by observing all the traffic rules and regulations and they reached near Jeeganahalli Cross, Anil Land between Mandikallu to Kammaguttahalli road, Chikkaballapura District, at that time a Tractor and Trailer bearing Reg.No.KA-40-TA-7552 and MF 241DI KA-40-TA-7551 which was driven by its driver on opposite direction came in a rash and negligent manner so as to endanger the human life and dashed against the deceased motorcycle.
Due to the terrific impact the husband and father of petitioners / deceased sustained grievous injuries all over his body.
Immediately after the accident he was rushed to Government Hospital, Chikkaballapura, but deceased was died on the way to the hospital.
Postmortem was conducted and corpse was handed over to the family members, who conducted funeral and other ceremonies by spending substantial amount.
The accident was caused due to the sole negligence of driver of Tractor and Trailer.
The respondents No.1 and 2 being the insurer and owner thereof are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.
3. The respondent No.1 filed objections statement denying the issuance of insurance policy in respect of Tractor and Trailer bearing Reg.No.KA-40-TA-7552 and MF 241DI- KA-40- TA-7551.
However the liability if any is pleaded to be subject to the terms and conditions of the policy.
The petition is bad for non-joinder of necessary parties.
This respondent specifically and empathically denied the occurrence, mode and manner of accident and also involvement of the vehicle in the accident.
Negligence on the part of the driver of its tractor and trailer is denied by this respondent.
Per contra it is alleged that the deceased was solely responsible for the alleged accident.
Without prejudice to the said contention it is averred that the driver of the Tractor and trailer did not possess valid & effective DL.
Despite knowing the said fact the owner thereof had handed over its possession to such a driver.

On account of willful breach of the terms & conditions of the policy by the insured,
the insurance company is not liable to indemnify him.
Further contended that the petitioners are called upon to prove their relationship and dependency with the deceased.
Non- compliance of Sec's 134(c), 159, 150 of the MV Act, 1988 is pleaded.
In fact deceased was also not wearing helmet at the time of alleged accident.
Further denied all the allegation made in the petition.
Hence prayed to dismiss the petition.

sentences.text: The only issue with which the parties are at loggerheads is with regard to the factum of negligence.
The petitioners plead that the driver of Tractor and Trailer bearing Reg.No.KA-40-TA-7552 and KA-40-TA-7551 was solely responsible for the occurrence of the accident.
Whereas the respondent No.1 and 2 contends that the unfortunate accident occurred due to the negligence of the rider of motorcycle / deceased.
10. Based on the FIS lodged by Mr.Gangadarappa - the pillion rider of the motorcycle set the criminal law into the motion by lodging Ex.P.2-First information statement.

Based on the said FIS,
the jurisdictional police registered FIR as per Ex.P.1, investigated the matter and laid charge sheet (Ex.P.12) against the driver of the Tractor and Trailer for the offences punishable u/s's 279, 337,
304(A) of IPC and U/s 181 of IMV Act.
But the point that merits consideration is that charge sheet is not conclusive proof of negligence.
It is incumbent upon this Tribunal to find out the truth independently without relying upon the charge sheet, more so when it is being seriously disputed by the insurance company.

11. According to the version of complainant in Ex.P.2 he clearly stated that he and deceased along with another person Venkateshappa were proceeding in a TVS Victor motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-03-ES-7366 from Mandikallu village towards Kammaguttahalli road and when they reached near Jeeganahalli cross at that time one Tractor and trailer coming from Jeeganahalli cross which was driven in rash and negligent manner had dashed the vehicle of the deceased.
On these allegations even the FIR is also lodged against the driver of the Tractor and Trailer bearing Reg.No.KA-40-TA-7551 as per Ex.P.1.
The sole contention of the respondents is that the charge sheet is filed against the insured vehicle i.e., Tractor and Trailer and as such police have not filed charge sheet against the deceased.
It is a trite law that a charge sheet is not an conclusive proof to come to the conclusion as to the negligence.
It is a settled principles of law that the tribunal has to assess the documentary and oral evidence and decide the factum of negligence independently.
With this prelude in the backdrop, let me navigate through the oral and documentary proof so as to found out the factum of negligence.
One of the document which sheds light on the factum of negligence is Ex.P.3 and 4 being the Spot Mahazar and spot sketch.
On careful perusal of Ex.P.3 and 4 it reflects that insured vehicle was going from Jiganahalli towards Mandikallu village.
The deceased and pillion riders went from Mandikallu towards Kammaguttahalli.
On careful perusal of Ex.P.4 there is cross from Jiganahlli towards Mandikallu.
The tractor and trailer driver had taken his vehicle from Jiganahalli towards Mandikallu i.e., from right side road.
He was on left side on the road.
The deceased and his pillion riders who were went to Kammaguttahalli went to their right side of the road.
It means they absolutely were going towards wrong side.
If they were going on the left side on the road, the accident could have avoided.
Further if the driver of the vehicle i.e. Tractor and trailer drove his vehicle slowly then also accident could have avoided.

Further the Ex.P.3 and 4 discloses that Tractor & trailer bearing Reg.KA-40-TA-7551 which came from the cross road to the main road and dashed the deceased motorcycle which was going on the straight road.
When this court navigates through the contents of Ex.P.3 & 4 it is forthcoming that the said road is 15 feet in width.
The deceased was going from Mandikallu to Kammaguttahalli.
The accident spot is just near to Jeeganahalli cross.
On perusal of the sketch it clearly reflects that the tractor and trailer was coming from cross road to main road on his lane from Jeeganahalli (Kammaguggattahalli road) towards MandiKallu.

Further the deceased along with 2 pillion riders were proceeding from Madikallu to Bayamma vs Universal Sampo Gen Ins Co Ltd on 10 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/194876373/
4 Kammaguttahalli road on the right side of the road.

sentences.text: If the deceased along with 2 pillion riders were proceeding in correct lane, the accident would have not occurred.
Further if the driver of the tractor and rider / deceased were coming in a normal speed then they would have certainly avoided the accident.

Another important aspect is to be noted herein the Handle, front wheel disc, front mud guard, head light, front both indicators, left side fuel tank, front both side mirror, front right side crash guard of the motorcycle was damaged and front bumper of the insured vehicle is damaged.
This categorically reveals that there is also negligence on the part of deceased and driver of insured tractor and trailer.

12. No doubt during the course of cross-examination PW.1 has admitted his father / deceased was rider of the two wheeler at the time of accident and he came to know that four persons were proceeding on the said two wheeler as on the date of accident.
But that itself is not enough to distrust the version of the claimants.
The contents of spot mahazar and spot sketch discloses that the respondent No.2 Tractor and Trailer driver had a clear vision as it is a straight road.
If the Tractor and Trailer driver was coming in a normal speed then he would have certainly avoided the accident.
There is a greater amount of negligence on the part of respondent No.2 Tractor and Trailer driver.
The police records are blatantly and blissfully silent as to negligence of the deceased.
Further it is also relevant to place reliance on the concept of last opportunity doctrine.
At this juncture it is also relevant to have the concept of doctrine of last opportunity.

The said doctrine is said to have emanated from the principle enunciated in Devies v. Mann (1842 (10) M&W 546) which has often been explained as amounting to a rule that when both parties are careless the party which has the last opportunity of avoiding the results of the other's carelessness is alone liable.
However, according to Lord Denning it is not a principle of law, but test of causation.

(See Davies v.
Swan Motor Co. (Swansea) Ltd. (1949 (2) KB 291).

sentences.text: Though in some decisions, the doctrine has been applied by courts, after the decisions of the House of Lords in The Volute (1922 (1) AC 129) and Swadling v. Cooper (1931 AC 1), it is no longer to be applied.
The sample test is what was the cause or what were the causes of the damage.

The act or omission amounting to want of ordinary care or in defiance of duty or obligation on the part of the complaining party which conjointly with the other party's negligence was the proximate cause of the accident renders it one to be the result of contributory negligence.
13. In the instant case on hand the respondent No.2 Tractor and Trailer driver had last opportunity to avoid the accident.
The occurrence of the accident on the relevant date, time and place is not in dispute.
The only issue with which the parties are at loggerheads is with regard to the factum of negligence.

On perusal of the evidence placed on record it reflects that, the driver / owner of the respondent No.2 Tractor and Trailer had hit the deceased's motorcycle on its right side that shows there is a negligence.

The factum of deceased along with 2 pillion riders were proceeding on a motorcycle on the wrong lane of the road without observing the vehicular movements show that even the deceased was also negligent.
14. No doubt the driver / owner of the respondent No.2 had a clear line of vision and could not have missed seeing the deceased motorcycle which was coming from straight.

But the very act of the respondent No.2 Tractor & Trailer hitting the motorcycle of the deceased itself depicts that he did Bayamma vs Universal Sampo Gen Ins Co Ltd on 10 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/194876373/
5 not exercise the degree of care which is expected of a prudent driver.

sentences.text: In this view of the matter lesser degree of negligence has to be attributed on the part of the deceased.
The driver of the respondent No.2 Tractor and Trailer by dashing the deceased motorcycle from right side had contributed a higher degree of negligence in the occurrence of the resultant accident.

The driver of the Tractor and Trailer who had failed to adhere to the basic rules & regulations and acted in a gross negligent manner on a village road without observing on coming vehicles had contributed a higher degree of negligence in the occurrence of the resultant accident.
15. In this view of the matter lesser degree of negligence has to be attributed on the part of the deceased.
Hence negligence is fixed on the driver of the Tractor and trailer & deceased/rider of motorcycle in the ratio of 60 : 40 respectively.

As such, I answer issue No.2 as 'Partly in the Affirmative'.
16. ISSUE NO.1:
The petitioners claim that, petitioner No.1 is the wife and petitioner No.2 & 3 are the major daughters of the deceased.
To prove the same, petitioner No.3 filed affidavit-in-lieu of her chief-examination and deposed about the above relationship.
The Aadhaar cards of petitioners and deceased at Ex.P.15 to 17 and contents of the police papers do fortify the said fact.
17. At this juncture, I would like to refer the decision reported in 2021 SCC Online Kerala 3209 (United India Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s. Shalumol and Others).

sentences.text:
In a recent decision in National Insurance Company Limited v.
Birender [(2020) 11 SCC 356], a claim petition filed by major married and earning sons of the deceased mother, the Honourable Supreme Court held as follows:
"12. The legal representatives of the deceased could move application for compensation by virtue of clause (c) of Section 166 (1).

Birender [(2020) 11 SCC 356]

sentences.text: The major married son who is also earning and not fully dependent on the deceased would be still covered by the expression "legal representative" of the deceased.

This Court in Manjuri Bera (supra)
had expounded that liability to pay compensation under the Act does not cease because of absence of dependency of the concerned legal representative.
Notably, the expression "legal representative" has not been defined in the Act.
14. It is thus settled by now that the legal representatives of the deceased have a right to apply for compensation.

Having said that, it must necessarily follow that even the major married and earning sons of the deceased being legal representatives have a right to apply for compensation and it would be the bounden duty of the Tribunal to consider the application irrespective of the fact whether the concerned legal representative was fully dependent on the deceased and not to limit the claim towards conventional heads only.

The evidence on record in the present case would Bayamma vs Universal Sampo Gen Ins Co Ltd on 10 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/194876373/
6 suggest that the claimants were working as agricultural labourers on contract basis and were earning meager income between Rs. 1,00,000/and Rs. 1,50,000/per annum.

sentences.text: In that sense, they were largely dependent on the earning of their mother and in fact, were staying with her, who met with an accident at the young age of 48 years."

18. Therefore, in view of the principles laid down by the Hon'ble High Court of Kerala and Hon'ble Supreme Court, which is referred in the above decision, this Tribunal is of the opinion that, the major married / earning sons and married daughters are also dependents to the deceased and they are entitled for the compensation under the motor vehicles accident cases.
It is pertinent to note that, this relationship of the petitioners with the deceased was not disputed by the respondents.

Since the evidence led by the petitioners is satisfactory and also taking into consideration the fact that there are no rival claimants, this Tribunal hold that the petitioners are the legal representatives of the deceased.
Therefore, petitioners are the legal heirs and dependents of deceased.
Hence, this Tribunal answers to issue No.1 In the Affirmative.
19. ISSUE NO.3 :
In this case the petitioners have claimed the compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- on the death of deceased in the road traffic accident.
The petitioners contended that, deceased was working as coolie and earning of Rs.25,000/-p.m.
In order to substantiate the above said fact absolutely no string of evidence is produced before this court.
It is relevant to rely on a decision of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka rendered on Division Bench in the case of Ananda v/s Arjun and another in MFA.No.101144/2020 (MV) dated.05.07.2023.

sentences.text:
Wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has laid down the following principles in para No.8(b) are as here under :
"(b) The accident is of the year 2017.
The Tribunal has assessed the income of the deceased at Rs.7,000/- per month as against the claim of Rs.2,50,000/- per annum.
To substantiate the said claim, the injured claimant has not placed any material on record, it is for the Courts and Tribunals to assess the income notionally.
The notional income fixed by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority for the accident of the year 2017 is Rs.10,250/-.

In the absence of any material produced by the claimant to prove his income, it is appropriate to assess the notional income of the injured claimant at Rs.10,250/- per month, and the same is assessed as the monthly income of the injured claimant"
As such this court is taking the notional income as prescribed by the Karnataka Legal Service Authority, Bengaluru.
Therefore in view of the above decision, the accident was occurred on 24.04.2023.
Therefore, Rs.16,000/- has to be taken into consideration as monthly income of the deceased.

20. So far as the age of the deceased is concerned, the petitioners have produced the Aadhar card to show the age of the deceased as per Ex.P13 wherein the date of birth of deceased is shown as 01.01.1975, which indicates that he was aged (48 years 3 months 23 days) 48 years on the date of accident.

Therefore the appropriate multiplier as per Sarla Verma's case for the said age group is '13'.

sentences.text: As per the decision of Hon'ble Apex Court reported in 2017 ACJ 2700 (SC) (National Insurance Company Limited Vs Pranay Sethi and others), if the person died in the motor accident, the income with respect to the future prospect has to taken into consideration while awarding compensation.

sentences.text: The Hon'ble Apex Court has provide the chart for age of the deceased and percentage for future prospects in between below the age of 40 years 40%, 40 years to 50 years 25% and 50 to 60 years 10%.
The deceased is not a permanent Employee and not a fixed salary person and he died at the age of 48 years.
Therefore, in this case, 25% income has to be taken into consideration for future prospects.

Further as stated above that, as on the date of accident, deceased aged about 48 years and as such, 25% is added to the income of the deceased, then it comes to Rs.20,000/- p.m.
(Rs.16,000/- + 4,000/- i.e. 25%).
22.
The deceased died living behind 3 dependents.

As per principle laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Sarala Verma Case, 1/3rd of his income is required to be deducted towards his personal expenses which comes to Rs.13,333/- p.m. (Rs.20,000 - Rs.6,667 = Rs.13,333/-).
23. The income of the deceased is taken as Rs.13,333/- p.m. and the multiplier '13' is applied, then the loss of dependency comes to Rs.20,79,948/- (Rs.13,333/- X 12 X 13).
Considering the above facts, this Tribunal deems it just and reasonable to grant for compensation of Rs.20,80,000/- under the head of loss of dependency.

24. Further, as Law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi and others, the compensation towards loss to estate, funeral expenses and consortium is to be awarded.

REGARDING INTEREST & LIABILITY:
Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% p.a is awarded it would meet the ends of justice.
28. There is no dispute with regard to the issuance of insurance policy and its validity as on the date of accident.

The controversy is with regard to the liability of the Insurance Company in the matter of indemnification on the ground that knowing fully well that he had no valid & effective driving licence to drive the vehicle, driver of the Tractor & Trailer drove the same in violation of the policy conditions and provisions of M.V. Act.
Admittedly the insurance policy was issued in respect of a offending vehicle.
But the contents of the charge sheet is available on record as on the date of the accident, the driver was not having driving licence to drove the Tractor and trailer.

29. While answering the issue No.1 this Tribunal comes to the conclusion that, accident occurred due to the negligence of the driver of the Tractor Trailer bearing Reg.No.KA-40-TA-7552 and KA-40-TA-7551.
The petitioners contended that the respondent No.1 is the insurer and respondent No.2 is the owner of the said vehicle hence they are jointly and severally liable to compensation.
The respondent No.1 denied the issuance of policy in respect of the offending vehicle.

The respondent No.1 contended that at the time of the accident the driver of the offending Tractor & Trailer was not holding driving license, hence it is violation of terms and conditions of the policy as such they are not liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.

Further it is pertinent to note that IO has given Notice u/s 133 of IMV Act as per Ex.P.6 and the said notice was replied as per Ex.P.7 wherein the owner of the offending Tractor and Trailer has admitted the involvement of the vehicle.
Further in his reply the details of DL column shows blank.
He further replied that at the time of accident the driver of the Tractor and Trailer was not having valid DL.
Hence it is clear that the respondent No.2 has violated the terms and conditions of the policy.
The charges are leveled against the owner of the Tractor and Trailer i.e., respondent No.2.
The respondent No.2 is the owner of the Tractor and Trailer and the said Tractor and Trailer was driven by the driver who does not have DL and he caused this accident.
Hence it is clear that the respondent No.2 has violated the terms and conditions of the policy.

Further it is clear that the respondent No.2 being owner cum driver Bayamma vs Universal Sampo Gen Ins Co Ltd on 10 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/194876373/

30. It is relevant to relied on the Citation No.FAO-1081- 2024 (O & M) in the case of Universal Sompo Gen.Ins.Co.Ltd. V/s Anuj Rani and other with respect to amendment of sec.150

sentences.text: and stated that the tribunal directed the appellant / Insurance company to pay the award amount to claimants and then to recover from driver / owner.

Further it is to be noted that in the said case that the accident took place on 27.05.2022 and the amendment to Motor Vehicles Act came into force w.e.f 01.04.2022.
31.
Reverting back to the factual matrix, this court also does not loose sight of the fact that, the accident had happened on 24.04.2023.
The amendment to the MV Act, came into force on 01.04.2022.
The amendment to Sec.150 of MV Act makes it crystal clear that, if a person drives a vehicle without DL, than there is no question of making insurance company liable.
Further the provision makes it clear that, there is no question of even pay and recovery also.
This accident is subsequent to that of the amendment to the IMV Act.
When such being the case, the Respondent No.1 cannot be made liable.

32. Further respondent No.1 has relied on the judgment of M.F.A.No.3297/2019 in the case of Smt.Adilakshmamma and Others Vs., Sri. Raju and other and contended that when the owner knowing fully well that he was not holding valid driving license to drive the Tractor and Trailer then the owner is liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.

sentences.text:
In this case on hand also the respondent No.2 is the owner of the Tractor and Trailer and he is knowing well that he did not possess valid DL caused this accident, hence the respondent No.1 is not liable to pay compensation to the petitioners,
but the respondent No.2 who is the owner of the Tractor and Trailer is liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
The said authority relied by the learned counsel for the respondent No.1 is applicable to the present case on hand.
As such the respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation.

Hence this issue is answered as 'Partly in the Affirmative'.
33. ISSUE NO.4 :

ORDER

The petition filed under Section 166 of M.V. Act 1988, is hereby partly allowed with costs in the following terms :

The respondent No.2

i.e. , the RC owner of the Tractor and Trailer bearing Reg.No.KA-40- TA-7551 and KA-40-TA-7552 is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of two months from the date of award.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Based on the said FIS,
the jurisdictional police registered FIR as per Ex.P.1, investigated the matter and laid charge sheet (Ex.P.12) against the driver of the Tractor and Trailer for the offences punishable u/s's 279, 337,
304(A) of IPC and U/s 181 of IMV Act.
The sole contention of the respondents is that the charge sheet is filed against the insured vehicle i.e., Tractor and Trailer and as such police have not filed charge sheet against the deceased.
It is a trite law that a charge sheet is not an conclusive proof to come to the conclusion as to the negligence.
It is a settled principles of law that the tribunal has to assess the documentary and oral evidence and decide the factum of negligence independently.
(See Davies v.
Swan Motor Co. (Swansea) Ltd. (1949 (2) KB 291).
13. In the instant case on hand the respondent No.2 Tractor and Trailer driver had last opportunity to avoid the accident.
The occurrence of the accident on the relevant date, time and place is not in dispute.
On perusal of the evidence placed on record it reflects that, the driver / owner of the respondent No.2 Tractor and Trailer had hit the deceased's motorcycle on its right side that shows there is a negligence.
The factum of deceased along with 2 pillion riders were proceeding on a motorcycle on the wrong lane of the road without observing the vehicular movements show that even the deceased was also negligent.
But the very act of the respondent No.2 Tractor & Trailer hitting the motorcycle of the deceased itself depicts that he did Bayamma vs Universal Sampo Gen Ins Co Ltd on 10 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/194876373/
5 not exercise the degree of care which is expected of a prudent driver.
In this view of the matter lesser degree of negligence has to be attributed on the part of the deceased.
The driver of the respondent No.2 Tractor and Trailer by dashing the deceased motorcycle from right side had contributed a higher degree of negligence in the occurrence of the resultant accident.
The driver of the Tractor and Trailer who had failed to adhere to the basic rules & regulations and acted in a gross negligent manner on a village road without observing on coming vehicles had contributed a higher degree of negligence in the occurrence of the resultant accident.
Since the evidence led by the petitioners is satisfactory and also taking into consideration the fact that there are no rival claimants, this Tribunal hold that the petitioners are the legal representatives of the deceased.
The deceased is not a permanent Employee and not a fixed salary person and he died at the age of 48 years.
25. In this case, the petitioner No.2 & 3 are the children of the deceased and as per the decision reported in (2018) 12 SCC 130 in the case of Magma General Insurance Company Limited V/s Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram and others, the petitioner No.2 & 3 are entitled for filial consortium, as the filial consortium is the right of the parents and children to get compensation in the case of an accidental death of a children and father as the case may be.
An accident leading to the death of a father cause great shock and agony to the children of the deceased and they lost their love and affection towards his/her father.
The petitioners contended that the respondent No.1 is the insurer and respondent No.2 is the owner of the said vehicle hence they are jointly and severally liable to compensation.
The respondent No.1 denied the issuance of policy in respect of the offending vehicle.
The respondent No.1 contended that at the time of the accident the driver of the offending Tractor & Trailer was not holding driving license, hence it is violation of terms and conditions of the policy as such they are not liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
knowing well that he was not holding driving license to drive the Tractor and trailer.
The amendment to Sec.150 of MV Act makes it crystal clear that, if a person drives a vehicle without DL, than there is no question of making insurance company liable.
Further the provision makes it clear that, there is no question of even pay and recovery also.
This accident is subsequent to that of the amendment to the IMV Act.
When such being the case, the Respondent No.1 cannot be made liable.
In this case on hand also the respondent No.2 is the owner of the Tractor and Trailer and he is knowing well that he did not possess valid DL caused this accident, hence the respondent No.1 is not liable to pay compensation to the petitioners,
but the respondent No.2 who is the owner of the Tractor and Trailer is liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
